title: The glory departed (1 Samuel 4)
hookLine: the ark is captured, Eli dies, and a baby is named "the glory is departed"

lines: A RUNNER WITH EARTH ON HIS HEAD.
BRING THE ARK, IT WILL SAVE US.
THE ARK OF GOD IS TAKEN.
cards: A runner comes from the battlefield with his clothes torn and earth on his head, and the whole city cries out. Eli, very old now, his eyes set so that he cannot see, sits on his seat by the road, waiting.
His heart, the text says, trembled for the ark of God.
Israel had lost a battle to the Philistines, and the elders had a plan: bring the ark of the covenant from Shiloh into the camp, so that it may come among us and save us.
When it arrived, the soldiers shouted until the earth rang. Now the runner reaches the old man. Israel has fled.

teach.b: It's the ark that breaks him.

When the runner names the ark, Eli falls backward from his seat by the gate, his neck breaks, and he dies. Then the chapter turns somewhere unexpected: not to the generals or the priests, but to a woman in labor.

The wife of Eli's son Phinehas hears it all at once: the ark taken, her father-in-law dead, her husband dead. The labor comes on her suddenly. The women attending her try to comfort her: fear not, you've borne a son.
She doesn't answer, and doesn't take it to heart. She has one thing left to do.
She names the child Ichabod, saying, "The glory is departed from Israel," because the ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
Then she says it again: the glory is departed from Israel; for the ark of God is taken. The elders carried the ark into battle so it would save them. It didn't.

teach.h: A MOTHER NAMES WHAT WAS LOST.
teach.b: In one day the ark is gone, the old priest is dead with his two sons, and the one who names it plainly is a dying mother, giving her son a name nobody would want.
And yet the book doesn't end here.

teach.h: THE GLORY IS DEPARTED FROM ISRAEL.
teach.b: In the chapters that follow, the ark's story goes on, and not the way the Philistines expected.

how: Jews read the loss of the ark at Aphek as part of the Former Prophets, and some readers take the elders' plan to carry the ark into battle as a warning against treating holy things as charms.

games.q: you're one of the elders. Israel has just lost a battle to the Philistines. what do you do?
o: pull back and ask why it went wrong.
bring the ark of the covenant into the camp so it will save you.
games.why: they bring the ark from Shiloh, the camp shouts so the earth rings, and the next battle is worse: the ark itself is taken.

practice: Let a loss of something bigger than you come to mind: a place that closed, a community that broke apart, a hope you carried for years.
Don't rush to the bright side; give it a true name, even just in your head, and let the naming be enough for now. If you pray, bring that loss to God exactly as it is.

wordCard.voice: Ichabod. The name a dying mother gives her son on the day the ark is taken and Eli dies: the glory is departed from Israel.

orig.note: Hebrew: Ichabod, the name the text explains with 'the glory is departed from Israel'.
